text.p: The Philippines reported a 16.6 percent increase in its merchandise export receipts during the first nine months of the year, the presidential palace said on Tuesday.
Receipts went up to $14.926 billion from $12.802 billion in the same period last year.
The biggest dollar-earner was electronics and components accounting for 40.9 percent of total receipts.
United States remained the main buyer of Philippine products with sales reaching $637.35 million in September, up from $584.29 million in the same month last year.
The second biggest importer in September was Japan, followed by the Netherlands, Singapore, Malaysia and Germany, the palace said.
The statement did not say which countries were the biggest importers of Philippine products over the nine-month period.
